mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 5% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY growth > 5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in one month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of periods following two consecutive quarters of GDPC1 decline, or GDPC1 decline does not correlate with subsequent earnings reductions.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in one month signals a strong supply-side response, which typically leads to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 2% does not correlate with subsequent economic activity.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) YoY growth is below 2%, the real interest rate is high, which typically leads to a slowdown in economic activity and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the specified condition does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in one month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or PAYEMS decrease > 100,000 does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% YoY and retail sales (RSAFS) are stagnant or declining, it signals a weakening demand environment, which leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% YoY and RSAFS stagnant/declining
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the specified condition does not correlate with subsequent earnings reductions.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.5% in one month signals an easing monetary policy, which typically leads to increased liquidity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent liquidity increases.
